title: Checkout latency with healthy checkout pods
prompt: Checkout p95 increased from 420 ms to 8.7 s at 16:42 UTC. Checkout pods are healthy and no deployment targeted checkout itself. Determine the originating fault and trace how it reaches checkout latency.

evidence.summary: Checkout latency rises without local saturation
evidence.content: checkout p95 rose to 8.7 s while CPU was 34%, memory 41%, queue depth 2, and pod restart count zero.

evidence.summary: Promotion lookup dominates slow checkout traces
evidence.content: Trace checkout/b19 total 9.1 s: inventory 38 ms, payment 91 ms, promotion ApplyDiscount 8.82 s across 15 repeated client spans.
promotion-service logged cache timeout attempts 1 through 15 for each ApplyDiscount request; retry delay is 500 ms and no overall deadline is set.

evidence.summary: Retry policy changed shortly before the incident
evidence.content: Config revision 771 changed promotion cache max_attempts from 2 to 15 and request_deadline_ms from 1200 to 0. Cache endpoint was unchanged.

evidence.summary: A brief cache latency event triggers retries
evidence.content: promotion-cache p99 rose to 620 ms for 70 seconds during shard rebalancing, then returned to 12 ms. Checkout latency stayed high until retrying requests drained.

evidence.summary: Orders database shows a small unrelated latency rise
evidence.content: orders database p95 moved from 17 ms to 31 ms, remaining below its 80 ms SLO; checkout traces spend under 45 ms in order writes.
promotion outbound pool active connections reached 100/100 and waiters reached 238 as long retry chains accumulated.
